verses.text: Paul, and Silas, and Timothy. To the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We are bound to thank God always for you, brothers, as it is meet (right). For your faith grows exceedingly. And the charity (love) of every one of you all toward each other abounds (overflows).

So we ourselves glory (brag) in you in the churches of God. We glory (brag) in your patience and faith. You have this in all your persecutions (being attacked for faith) and tribulations (troubles) that you endure.
This is a manifest token (clear sign) of the righteous (right) judgment of God. It shows that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God. You also suffer for that kingdom.
It is a righteous (right) thing with God to recompense (pay back) tribulation (trouble) to those who trouble you.
And to you who are troubled, God will give rest with us. This will be when the Lord Jesus will be revealed (shown) from heaven with His mighty angels,

In flaming fire taking vengeance (paying back) on those who do not know God. He will take vengeance (paying back) on those who do not obey the gospel (good news). That is the gospel (good news) of our Lord Jesus Christ.
They will be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord. They will be punished from the glory of His power.
This will be when He will come to be glorified (praised) in His saints (holy people). He will be admired in all those who believe in that day. This is because our testimony among you was believed.

So we pray always for you. We pray that our God would count you worthy of this calling. We pray God would fulfil all the good pleasure of His goodness. We pray He would fulfil the work of faith with power.
Then the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified (praised) in you. And you may be glorified (honored) in Him. This is according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.text: Now we beseech (beg) you, brothers, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. We beseech (beg) you by our gathering together to Him,
Do not be soon shaken in mind, or troubled. Do not be troubled by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us. Do not be troubled as if the day of Christ is at hand (near).

Let no one deceive (fool) you by any means. For that day will not come, except there come a falling away (many people turning away from God) first. And that man of sin must be revealed (shown), the son of perdition (one headed for destruction).
That man opposes and exalts (lifts up) himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped. That man sits in the temple of God as God. And he shows himself that he is God.
Do you not remember that I told you these things when I was still with you?
And now you know what withholds (holds back). It holds back so that the man of sin might be revealed (shown) in his time.
For the mystery (secret) of iniquity (sin) does already work. Only he who now lets (holds back) will let (hold back), until he is taken out of the way.
And then that Wicked one will be revealed (shown). The Lord will consume him with the spirit of His mouth. The Lord will destroy him with the brightness of His coming.
The Wicked one's coming is after the working of Satan. That one will come with all power and signs and lying wonders,
And with all deceivableness (trickery) of unrighteousness (wrong) in those who perish. This is because they did not receive the love of the truth. By it they might have been saved.
For this cause God will send them strong delusion (a powerful lie). Then they should believe a lie.
Then all might be damned (condemned) who did not believe the truth. They had pleasure in unrighteousness (wrong).

But we are bound to give thanks always to God for you. You are brothers beloved (dearly loved) of the Lord. For God has from the beginning chosen you to salvation. He chose you through sanctification (being made holy) of the Spirit and belief of the truth.
God called you to this by our gospel (good news). He called you to the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore, brothers, stand fast. Hold the traditions (teachings handed down) which you have been taught, whether by word, or by our epistle (letter).
Now our Lord Jesus Christ Himself, and God, even our Father, has loved us. God has given us everlasting consolation (comfort) and good hope through grace.
May they comfort your hearts, and stablish (make firm) you in every good word and work.

verses.text: Finally, brothers, pray for us. Pray that the word of the Lord may have free course (spread quickly). Pray that it may be glorified (honored), even as it is with you.
And pray that we may be delivered (rescued) from unreasonable (wrong-headed) and wicked men. For not all people have faith.
But the Lord is faithful. He will stablish (make firm) you, and keep you from evil.
And we have confidence in the Lord touching (about) you. We trust that you both do and will do the things which we command you.
And may the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God. May He direct them into the patient waiting for Christ.

Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Withdraw yourselves from every brother who walks disorderly (out of line). Withdraw from any who do not walk after the tradition (teaching) which they received from us.
For you yourselves know how you ought to follow us. For we did not behave ourselves disorderly (out of line) among you.
Neither did we eat anyone's bread for nothing. We wrought (worked) with labour (hard work) and travail (toil) night and day. We did this so that we might not be chargeable (a cost) to any of you.
It is not because we have not power (the right). It is to make ourselves an ensample (example) to you to follow us.
For even when we were with you, this we commanded you: If anyone would not work, neither should they eat.
For we hear that there are some who walk among you disorderly (out of line). They do not work at all, but are busybodies (meddlers).
Now we command and exhort (encourage) such people by our Lord Jesus Christ. With quietness let them work, and eat their own bread.
But you, brothers, do not be weary in well doing (doing good).
And if anyone does not obey our word by this epistle (letter), note that person. Have no company with them, so that they may be ashamed.
Yet do not count them as an enemy, but admonish (warn) them as a brother.
Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace always by all means. The Lord be with you all.
I Paul write the salutation (greeting) with my own hand. This is the token (sign) in every epistle (letter). So I write.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
